title: Grateful Dead Live at St. Paul Civic Center on 1982-08-06

ai_review.summary: A scorching 21‑song Minnesota show captured on an audience tape that sounds surprisingly crisp and brings the band’s high‑octane energy straight to the listener.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about this early‑'80s St. Paul performance, calling it a "monster" set with nonstop fire—from a blistering Scarlet Begonias → Fire on the Mountain to a tight Lost Sailor → Saint of Circumstance and an inspired Candyman. The audience recording is praised for its front‑row feel, clear instrumental balance (with only a slight boominess) and captures the band’s sweaty, high‑energy vibe, though listeners note Phil’s bass could be boosted a touch in the mix.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen enthusiastic 4–5 star reviews consistently highlight both an exceptional performance and a surprisingly high‑quality audience recording, with only minor technical quibbles.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audience tape recorded from near the stage (behind the drums); crisp overall with slight boominess and a modest need to raise Phil’s bass in the mix. No major dropouts reported.

standout_songs: Scarlet Begonias > Fire on the Mountain
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows seamlessly, maintaining high momentum from the opening Bertha through a series of tightly linked jams and transitions, culminating in an electrifying second half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Strong vocal inflections on Candyman; his guitar "sizzles" during Fire on the Mountain and spacey jam sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is powerful, leads the transition from Scarlet into Fire, and generally drives the groove; listeners suggest turning him up a bit in the mix.
